source: Local time-class gate -- machine load, compiler and background processes move these numbers; NOT in CTest (AGENTS.md 4.4 rule 21: bench, not assertion). Run tools/check/check_perf_gates.ps1 to judge a build against this file.
note: The absolute lines come from SPEC.NF.PERF.02 (cat 10 MB >= 45 fps; full redraw <= 100 ms) and the relative line (max_regression_percent) is that requirement's own 'regression > 10% is FAIL'. Metric keys are exactly those the bench writes under "metrics" in its --json= output. direction names the better side. A gate with relative=false is judged only by its absolute line.

capture.aggregation: median across runs -- the same rule the gate applies, so a reference and a reading are comparable
capture.build: msvc preset (Ninja + MSVC), default config (dracula, Cascadia 14pt)

ungated.reason: Ingestion throughput, not per-frame render cost. It is currently limited by the write side (each fed chunk re-scans the whole viewport for dirty rows), which is a known defect under investigation; gating it here would freeze that defect in as the contract. Render cost under the same load is gated by B-5 / B-6.
Derivative of scroll_frame_ms_mean (1000 / mean); gating both would double-count one signal.
Count of measured frames, a sample-size diagnostic rather than a cost.

gates.note: SPEC.NF.PERF.02's named metric: 10 MB fed through cat must hold >= 45 fps.
The three capture runs spanned 9.8-15.1 ms (54%), wider than a 10% window, so a relative line here would read red on environment jitter. Only the requirement's absolute line judges it.
One row dirty per frame: the cheapest view of the per-frame cost of dirty-row filtering, run splitting and colour resolution.
Tail of B-3; unusually stable in the capture (8.03-8.14 ms), so the tail is worth locking.
Frame cost while the 10 MB feed is in flight (whole-viewport dirty plus concurrent producer thread).
Tail under load; the capture spanned 13.5-16.8 ms, so median aggregation matters here.
